discovery: Invention and development of silicon pixel detectors for precision tracking and imaging of charged particles
motivation: Silicon pixel detectors turned tracking from projected strips into true three-dimensional, micron-scale imaging of particle trajectories in very high-rate environments. Heijne pioneered planar silicon sensors at CERN and the hybrid pixel concept, with bump-bonded readout chips, that later led to the Medipix photon-counting imagers. Parker developed monolithic pixel sensors and, with colleagues, 3D silicon sensors with electrodes etched through the bulk, giving the radiation hardness and speed that the LHC inner layers need. Snoeys led the development of monolithic CMOS active pixel sensors, culminating in the ALPIDE chip of ALICE's 10-square-metre tracker. Pixel vertex detectors made it possible to identify b-quarks and tau leptons among thousands of tracks, which was essential for the top-quark and Higgs-boson programmes, including the observation of H to bb. The same technology now underpins X-ray imaging, medical diagnostics and the 4D trackers planned for future colliders.
